policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 5:1 'The elders therefore among you I exhort' renders the connective οὖν; the RP reading substitutes the article τοὺς, which the ASV's 'therefore' does not represent.

ASV 5:2 prints 'exercising the oversight' in its text, and the mapped textual_variant note ('Some ancient authorities omit exercising the oversight') marks the omission as the other authorities' reading, not the ASV's.

ASV 5:2 prints 'according to the will of God' in its text, with the mapped textual_variant note ('Some ancient authorities omit according to the will of God') assigning the omission to other authorities.

ASV 5:5 has only one expression of subjection ('be subject unto the elder') and renders ἀλλήλοις with 'to serve one another'; no second participle 'being subject one to another' appears, so the RP addition ὑποτασσόμενοι is unrepresented. The note here is alternative_rendering and only redistributes the English phrase.

ASV 5:8 'seeking whom he may devour' requires the pronoun, excluding the omission (r02), but the indefinite τινα and interrogative τίνα differ only by accent and yield the same English, so the ASV does not distinguish them.

ASV 5:8 'seeking whom he may devour' is a natural rendering of either the infinitive καταπιεῖν or the subjunctive καταπίῃ; the English modal 'may devour' does not distinguish the Greek forms and no note is mapped here.

ASV 5:9 'in the world' needs the English article whether or not the Greek τῷ is present, so the wording does not distinguish the readings; the only mapped notes are an alternative_rendering ('Or, the') and greek_gloss notes, neither of which decides a reading.
ASV 5:10 reads 'in Christ' with no 'Jesus'; the Treg/NA/RP addition Ἰησοῦ would appear as 'in Christ Jesus'.
ASV 5:10 'shall himself perfect, establish, strengthen you' renders the future indicative καταρτίσει in a series of futures; the RP optative καταρτίσαι ὑμᾶς would give a wish ('may he perfect you').

ASV 5:10 has only three verbs, 'perfect, establish, strengthen', and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities add settle' places θεμελιώσει outside the ASV's text, so the ASV follows the omission.
ASV 5:11 'To him be the dominion for ever and ever' ascribes only dominion; the RP addition ἡ δόξα καὶ would read 'the glory and the dominion'.
ASV 5:11 'for ever and ever', glossed 'Greek unto the ages of the ages', renders the doubled τῶν αἰώνων; the omission would yield only 'for ever'.
ASV 5:12 'stand ye fast therein' is an imperative rendering the aorist imperative στῆτε; the RP perfect indicative ἑστήκατε would give a relative clause 'wherein ye stand'.
ASV 5:14 ends 'that are in Christ.' with neither 'Jesus' nor a closing 'Amen', both of which the RP addition Ἰησοῦ ἀμήν would supply.
